_comment: Profane crimes (systems/profaneCrimes.js): a rival House's crypt broken and its dead scattered, holy relics stolen, sold to another faith or faked, and a healer or old woman cried witch for what she owns. Tuning and prose. Feud/standing/karma are signed deltas; chances are 0..1 per roll.

crypt._comment: The crypt of a rival House at its seat (house.rivals[k].seat). goods: grave goods laid with the dead (each funeral after the first adds funeralGoods, paid from the House's purse at funeralGoodGold apiece); bones: sets of bones lying there.

relics._comment: Relics held in player.profane.relics. A temple's reliquary holds stockRange relics (by a hash of the town). price: what a temple pays (× the realm's piety / 50, clamped by pietyMult). Fakes: bones + gold for a gilt box; quality from intelligence and craft.

witch._comment: Crying witch on a townswoman: a healer (job 'healer') or a woman of oldAge or more. The trial: convict chance; the mob: always kills, takes only the purse. What is seized: her purse (accuserShare to the player, the rest to the town's purse) and her land (a lot she holds, else a free lot of the town granted to the accuser), as the realm's law allows.
witch.mobCause: killed by a mob, cried a witch

relics: a thorn from the crown of Saint {saint}

lines.cryptRob: You force the crypt of {house} by night and take {goods} grave goods from beside their dead.
lines.cryptScatter: You break open the crypt of {house}, pull its dead from their niches and scatter the bones of their fathers across the floor. You carry off {bones} sets of bones.
lines.cryptSeen: You were seen. By morning all {town} knows whose hand it was, and so will {house}.
lines.cryptUnseen: No one saw. {house} will find the crypt broken, and wonder.
lines.cryptLearned: {house} has learned whose hand broke the crypt of their fathers. They will not forget it.
lines.cryptNewHead: {head}, new head of {house}, swears over the bones of the fathers that your House will pay.
lines.cryptRebury: You bring the bones back to the crypt of {house} and pay for a requiem. It does not undo it; it was done.
lines.chronicleScatter: {ruler} broke the crypt of {house} at {town} and scattered the bones of their fathers.
lines.relicStolen: You lift {relic} from the reliquary of {town}'s temple.
lines.relicCaught: A sexton sees you at the reliquary. The relic is taken back, you are fined {fine}g, and the priests will remember your face.
lines.relicSold: The priests of {faith} at {town} pay {gold}g for {relic}.
lines.relicBetrayal: You have sold a relic of your own faith to the priests of another god.
lines.relicBetrayalFound: Word comes back: you sold {relic} to the priests of {faith}. Your own clergy will not soon forgive it.
lines.fakeMade: Bones from the charnel, a gilt box and a story: {relic}. It might pass.
lines.fakeExposed: The priests of {town} have found out {relic} for a fake. They want {fine}g back, and the realm has heard of it.
lines.fakeExposedPaid: The priests of {town} found out {relic} for a fake; {fine}g is taken from your purse in restitution.
lines.fakeExposedUnpaid: The priests of {town} found out {relic} for a fake. You could not pay them back, and {realm} will remember it.
lines.chronicleFakeExposed: {ruler} was found out selling a false relic to the temple at {town}.
lines.witchCondemned: The priest hears the charge and the town finds against her. {name} is {cause}. Her purse ({coin}g) is seized: {share}g to you as her accuser, the rest to the town.
lines.witchNoLand: The realm's law will not let you hold the land; the town keeps it.
lines.witchAcquitted: The priest will not have it. {name} walks free, and the whole town knows you cried witch on her.
lines.witchMob: You cry witch in the street and the street answers. {name} is {cause}. You take {share}g of her purse; the mob takes the rest.
lines.chronicleWitch: {ruler} cried witch on {name} of {town}, and she was {cause}.
lines.chronicleWitchAcquitted: {ruler} cried witch on {name} of {town}; the priest acquitted her.
